answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable bond in a scarce token before it can submit jobs or claim rewards. A reputation-weighted contract then releases payment only after independent counterparties confirm delivery; proven fraud forfeits the bond, while creating more identities does not multiply a single bond’s voting weight. This makes a sybil campaign costly: the attacker must lock capital across many identities and risks losing it when caught. At the summit, onyx validators can anchor the bond rule in the protocol.
